prompt.text: Elizabeth Hargrave's 2019 hit about attracting birds to your wildlife preserve.
Wingspan players store food tokens in a dice tower shaped like this backyard object.
Wingspan's base deck has 170 cards, each depicting a unique bird from this continent.
In 2019 Wingspan won this "expert" sibling of the Spiel des Jahres.
Hargrave built Wingspan's bird data starting from this free Cornell-affiliated citizen-science database she used as a birder.

items.source: Hargrave interviews (meeplemountain.com) - confirm exact phrasing pre-event

prompt.text: Wingspan won the 2019 Kennerspiel under this German name, meaning "wing beat".
Wingspan's first expansion added 81 new birds from this continent, including the common swift and Eurasian magpie.

items.source: Stonemaier store page + Wingsplain card list, both confirming 81 European bird cards (verified 2026-08-13)

prompt.text: This 2022 Spiel des Jahres winner by Randy Flynn has players tiling a Pacific Northwest ecosystem with bears, salmon and elk.
Cascadia's title refers to a bioregion of this corner of North America.

items.source: Wikipedia. Ordering constraint: must stay BELOW the Cascadia clue - its text spoils this answer if reversed

prompt.text: In Photosynthesis, a rotating 3D version of this celestial object determines which trees score light points.
Mathias Wigge's 2021 heavyweight Ark Nova has you building one of these institutions while funding conservation projects.
Terraforming Mars corporations raise Mars' temperature, oxygen and this third global parameter measured in ocean tiles.

items.source: Terraforming Mars rules - confirm exact rulebook wording pre-event

prompt.text: Keymaster Games' PARKS uses artwork licensed from this print series that commissioned poster artists for each US national park.
Living Forest, about protecting a forest from fire, won this award in 2022 - the same year Cascadia took the family prize.
Established 1872, it's the first national park in the US (and by most accounts, the world).
With 12.2 million visits in 2024 - nearly triple #2 Zion - it's perennially America's most-visited national park.

items.source: NPS 2024 visitation data. RECHECK: 2025 numbers likely published by event night

prompt.text: At 13.2 million acres - six Yellowstones - this Alaska park is America's largest.
Kentucky's Mammoth Cave is the world's longest known cave system, with more than this many miles mapped (nearest hundred).

items.source: NPS. RECHECK: survey teams add mapped miles every year

prompt.text: Old Faithful erupts about every 90 minutes; rangers predict eruptions within plus-or-minus 10 minutes with about this accuracy.

items.source: nps.gov. RECHECK: NPS occasionally revises the prediction stats

prompt.text: At 1,943 feet, this Oregon caldera lake is the deepest in the United States.

items.source: NPS. CONFLICT: answer duplicates picture cell img-04 - use only if that image is swapped out

prompt.text: Death Valley's Furnace Creek officially recorded Earth's hottest temperature, 134 degrees Fahrenheit, in this decade - though many meteorologists now dispute the reading.

items.source: WMO official record; disputed per 2026 BAMS study - host MUST say "officially recorded" (pool flag 7)

prompt.text: The largest animal ever known to live - its tongue can weigh as much as an elephant.
Fastest animal on Earth: this raptor's hunting dive has been measured at 242 mph.
A blue whale's 400-lb heart pumps roughly this many gallons of blood per beat - a bathtub's worth.
A 2016 Science study of eye-lens radiocarbon found this Arctic shark is the longest-lived vertebrate - at least 272 years.

items.source: Science (2016). CONFLICT: if Final alternate B is chosen, swap this cell to bench h-51

prompt.text: Monarch butterflies fly up to 3,000 miles to overwinter in Mexico's forests of this "sacred fir".
The monarchs that reach Mexico have never been there - they're roughly this many generations removed from the ones that left.
Before Mario, this company was founded in Kyoto in 1889 to make hanafuda - Japanese "flower cards".

items.source: Britannica. Host note: say "Nintendo says 1889" if challenged (pool flag 11)

prompt.text: Found in 4,600-year-old Mesopotamian tombs, this 20-square racing game is often called the oldest playable board game.

items.source: British Museum. Host note: phrase as "oldest with surviving rules" if challenged (pool flag 10)

prompt.text: Boards for this Egyptian game of passing into the afterlife appear as far back as ~3100 BC and were buried with Tutankhamun.
In 1904, Lizzie Magie patented this anti-monopolist teaching game - three decades before Parker Brothers sold a suspiciously similar product.

items.source: Smithsonian. Round 1 Double-Down: the story payoff cell

prompt.text: Magie sold her patent to Parker Brothers for just this much - no royalties - while Charles Darrow got rich on "his" invention.

items.source: history.com. CONFLICT: keep at most two of the Magie/Darrow trio (l-73, l-74, q-102) in one game

prompt.text: Hanafuda decks have 48 cards in 12 suits representing these.

answer.canonical: Months of the year (flowers of each month)

prompt.text: Hanafuda cards are still sold by Nintendo today, including a deck themed on this mustachioed mascot.
Alan R. Moon's 2004 Spiel des Jahres winner about claiming railway routes.
Working alone for four-plus years as "ConcernedApe", Eric Barone built this farming game - art, code and music included.
This German dental technician designed Catan in his basement lab; it won the 1995 Spiel des Jahres.
Coined during a 2000 Carcassonne session as a mash-up of "my" and "people", it's now the generic word for wooden board game figures.
Tetris creator who programmed the original in 1984 while working at the Soviet Academy of Sciences.

items.source: CNN / Wikipedia. Mild thematic echo with Games in Spaaace - no duplicate answers, fine

prompt.text: She turned birding spreadsheets into 2019's Wingspan.

items.source: meeplemountain.com. CONFLICT: only usable if the Birds, Meeples & Eggs category is cut

prompt.text: Alan Moon won the Spiel des Jahres twice: Ticket to Ride in 2004 and this fantasy travel game in 1998.
Per Guinness, this puzzle game became the first video game in space when cosmonaut Aleksandr Serebrov packed a Game Boy for his 1993 Mir mission.
On June 9, 1970, Soyuz 9 cosmonauts played the first space-vs-Earth match of this classic game - a draw after ~6 hours and 4 orbits.
Serebrov's space-flown Game Boy was later auctioned for about this much - famously modest - at a 1996 Sotheby's Russian space sale.

items.source: Sotheby's-related coverage. Round 2 Double-Down #1: the anti-climax is the joke

prompt.text: The Soyuz 9 chess set was purpose-built for weightlessness with pieces that did this, to keep them from floating away.
Serebrov's Game Boy rode Soyuz TM-17 to Mir and spent this long aboard - just shy of 200 days.
Tetris was born in 1984 at the Soviet Academy of Sciences, programmed by Alexey Pajitnov on this Soviet PDP-11 clone whose display drew pieces from bracket characters.
Guinness credits Tetris's space flight to this cosmonaut.

items.source: Guinness ("First person to play a videogame in space"). Doubles as row 5 of alternate category Video Game Firsts; unusable if Final alternate C is chosen

prompt.text: Released March 20, 2020 - days before lockdowns - this Nintendo island-life game sold 11.77 million copies in 12 days.
Free Lives' 2023 game Terra Nil is called a "reverse" one of these - you restore a wasteland to wilderness, then remove every trace of yourself.
In this 2022 survival game you play Earth's last mother fox protecting cubs; its subtitle is "Extinction is Forever".
E-Line Media's ocean game Beyond Blue was inspired by this BBC documentary series' second season.
ustwo games planted one tree per download of this 2020 wildlife-photography adventure set on a Spanish island - topping 1 million trees by Dec 2021.

items.source: ustwo / Ecologi ("Alba's Forest", 1,086,067 trees funded - historical, stable)

prompt.text: Never Alone (Kisima Ingitchuna), starring a girl and an arctic fox, was co-developed with the Cook Inlet Tribal Council to share the folklore of this Alaska Native people.
In Animal Crossing, donating fish, fossils and bugs to this owl curator builds your island's museum.
Terra Nil's endgame twist: after restoring the ecosystem you must do this to your own buildings.

items.source: Steam / PC Gamer. CONFLICT: near-duplicate of the boarded Terra Nil clue (c-13) - use one or the other

prompt.text: At about 52,500 cubic feet of trunk, this Sequoia NP giant is the largest living tree on Earth by volume.

items.source: nps.gov/seki. Host note: say "largest TREE by volume" - Pando and the humongous fungus are larger organisms (pool flag 9)

prompt.text: General Sherman is this species - Sequoiadendron giganteum.
Scientists estimate General Sherman's age at roughly this many years - old enough to predate the Roman Empire's peak.
The world's TALLEST tree, this ~380-ft coast redwood in Redwood National Park, beats General Sherman's height by over 100 feet.

items.source: Guinness. RECHECK exact height (381.3 ft per recent measurement)

prompt.text: Visit Hyperion and you risk 6 months in jail and a $5,000 fine - the park closed access in 2022 because visitors were damaging this part of the tree's ecosystem.

items.source: NPR / CNN, Redwood NP statement. RECHECK closure still in force

prompt.text: This national park's namesake trees are the largest on Earth by volume; its neighbor Kings Canyon shares an entrance sign.
Pando, ~47,000 genetically identical aspen trunks sharing one root system in Utah's Fishlake National Forest, is arguably Earth's heaviest single organism at about this many tons.

items.source: National Forest Foundation. RESERVED: do NOT board while Final A (Pando) is the final - it spoils the answer

prompt.text: Pando is Latin for this - fitting for a clone that's covered 106 acres.

items.source: National Forest Foundation. RESERVED: do NOT board while Final A (Pando) is the final - it IS the final clue's hook

prompt.text: By preying on kelp-munching sea urchins, this marine mammal is the textbook "keystone species" of Pacific kelp forests.
Critically endangered in the wild since 2006, axolotls are everywhere in labs and pet stores - and in this Mojang game, where blue ones are ultra-rare.

items.source: IUCN; Minecraft wiki. RECHECK blue-variant odds (1/1200) if cited aloud - game updates can change spawn logic

prompt.text: The world's most endangered marine mammal: this tiny Gulf of California porpoise numbered only ~7-10 individuals in the 2025 survey.

items.source: NOAA / Sea Shepherd. RECHECK count week-of - the most volatile number on the board

prompt.text: This flightless, nocturnal New Zealand parrot fell to ~51 birds in 1995; intensive recovery has it back over 200.

items.source: NZ Department of Conservation. RECHECK count (~230-240) - updated after breeding seasons

prompt.text: In 2025, scientists celebrated when 18 captive-bred axolotls did this in restored Xochimilco wetlands - a first hopeful sign for reintroduction.

answer.canonical: Survive after release into the wild

prompt.text: Wild axolotls survive only in this Mexico City lake system, a UNESCO site of "floating gardens".
This bird is the world's only flightless parrot and can weigh 4 kilograms.

items.source: NZ DOC. CONFLICT: same answer as the boarded kakapo clue (i-53) - use only as its replacement. Also benches alternate category Weird Nature

prompt.text: In April 2014, excavators in Alamogordo, NM confirmed the legend: Atari really did bury hundreds of thousands of cartridges of this 1982 movie flop.
In 2020, programmer Foone got Doom playable on the shell of this single-use medical device (with a replaced CPU and OLED screen).

items.source: PC Gamer / Gizmodo. Host note: phrase honestly - only the shell was original

prompt.text: During WWII, Britain's MI9 smuggled silk escape maps, compasses and currency to POWs inside sets of this board game.

items.source: Snopes-confirmed TRUE / UCSB Geography. Round 2 Double-Down #2: sounds fake, is not

prompt.text: Silk was used for the escape maps because paper maps fail in these two ways.

accepted: they rustle and dissolve when wet

prompt.text: The 2014 Atari dig recovered about this many cartridges of the ~700,000+ buried.
The 1935 "rags-to-riches inventor" story Parker Brothers told about this man is now considered myth - Lizzie Magie got there 30 years earlier.

items.source: Smithsonian / history.com. CONFLICT: same story arc as the Round 1 Magie cells (l-73/l-74) - swap in only if those are cut

prompt.text: Named with the Latin for "I spread", this 106-acre Utah resident may be the heaviest single organism on Earth.

items.source: National Forest Foundation. Final A (top pick): crossover-neutral, gasp-factor; f-37/f-38 stay benched so nothing on either board spoils it

prompt.text: A 2016 study of eye-lens proteins showed this Arctic fish species can live roughly 400 years - meaning some alive today predate the United States.

items.source: Science (2016). Final alternate B. CONFLICT: requires swapping h-49 off the Round 1 board (replace with bench h-51)

prompt.text: In 1993 this game became the first ever played in space; the Game Boy that carried it aboard Mir later sold at auction for just $1,220.

items.source: Guinness. Final alternate C (owner's sentimental favorite). CONFLICT: requires replacing all of Games in Spaaace with alternate category Video Game Firsts, minus its space clues

prompt.text: Pokemon creator Satoshi Tajiri was nicknamed "Dr. Bug" as a kid for this hobby, which inspired the whole franchise.
This 2016 mobile game sent millions outdoors hunting virtual creatures; park agencies issued off-trail warnings.

items.source: General knowledge - do not cite a specific-park anecdote without verifying

prompt.text: Tajiri said watching two kids connect Game Boys with this accessory made him imagine insects crawling along it.
In 2021, three rare Australian beetles in genus Binburrum were named articuno, zapdos and this - completing the trio.
The beetle-naming researchers chose Legendary Pokemon names for this reason.

answer.canonical: The beetles' rarity (like the Legendary birds)

prompt.text: Twitch Plays Pokemon (Feb-Mar 2014) set a Guinness record when this many people - over a million - helped input commands to beat Pokemon Red.
The 2019 Ig Nobel Physics Prize went to researchers who explained why this Australian marsupial's poop is cube-shaped.

items.source: Ig Nobel / UGA. Backup Double-Down candidate if boarded - move to a deeper row

prompt.text: Turritopsis dohrnii is called "the immortal" one of these - it can revert from adult back to its polyp stage.

items.source: AMNH. Also borrowable as an Animal Record Holders bench if this category is unused

prompt.text: The cubes come from varying stiffness in the wombat's ~10-meter-long version of this organ.
Old Faithful blasts boiling water up to this height - taller than the Statue of Liberty's copper figure.
The jellyfish's cellular reset - mature cells transforming into other cell types - is called this.
Three Minnesota student teachers created this 1971 educational classic; generations have "died of dysentery" since.
First game in space (1993, Game Boy, Mir).

items.source: Guinness. CONFLICT: only usable if Games in Spaaace is cut AND Final alternate C is not used

prompt.text: In October 1958 physicist William Higinbotham demoed "Tennis for Two" on an oscilloscope at this national laboratory.

items.source: bnl.gov. Host note: never say "first video game" flatly (pool flag 1)

prompt.text: The first video game patent - 1948's "Cathode-Ray Tube Amusement Device" - was inspired by this WWII display technology.
First single video game to sell 300 million copies (2023).

items.source: BBC / Forbes. RECHECK + host must say "single game", not franchise (pool flag 8)

prompt.text: Minecraft's creator sold Mojang to Microsoft in 2014 for this amount.
Catan has sold over this many copies in ~40 languages (nearest 10 million).

items.source: NPR / catan.com. RECHECK - volatile sales total

prompt.text: Games Done Quick's twice-yearly speedrun marathons have raised over $60 million total for these two main charities.

answer.canonical: Prevent Cancer Foundation and Doctors Without Borders

items.source: gamesdonequick.com. RECHECK total and current charity pair

prompt.text: Animal Crossing: New Horizons' first-12-days sales figure that made it the fastest-selling Switch game ever.

items.source: Nintendo Life. CONFLICT: near-duplicate of the boarded ACNH clue (c-18) - do not run both cells live

prompt.text: Xeno-canto, the citizen-science bird-sound archive, passed this recording milestone in 2024 - a nice round number.

media.alt: A geyser erupting in a steaming basin, viewed from a hillside overlook
A sheer granite dome rising above a forested valley
A freestanding red sandstone arch on a slickrock rim
A deep blue lake filling a volcanic caldera, with a cone-shaped island
Rippled white gypsum dunes under an evening sky
Aerial view of a rainbow-colored hot spring ringed by orange bacterial mats
A vast snow-covered mountain massif under clear skies
An amphitheater of orange rock spires seen from the rim

body.description: Every clue for the Board Game Club x Environmental Law Society night: both boards, the final with two alternates, the full bench, and four drop-in alternate categories. Environment + gaming only, nothing law-related. Assembled from docs/content/event-board-draft.md; per-clue source notes inline; volatile facts tagged recheck.
